sol.problem:
Skipping a zero Repeat in Facts does not undo its compiler-environment effects. Exact memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[0],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Function, with final LF:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
regs {  } bounds {0}
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
qloop 0 {
qfree c
c = qalloc any 2
}
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree c
Independently hashed H=c9cbc01c190e4454e37b553e1d7e8e9eeea856631a6ab397029577447b053b87 and canonical sole-symbol object_hash=708531c08cb63447ea2bbaa966c69562300ab1bc89e07efb9c3278799c54922d. check and run-action a --mut 0 actually exit 1, empty stdout, '§3.3: c must be one wire'. The zero-trip body executes no release or allocation: the original one-wire c remains clean, CX(c,b) is disabled and the full action is identity on t and bR. The ordinary §6 validator correctly validates the dead body in a cloned state. Borrow Compiler::compile instead compiles that body against self, calls produce(c,2), and leaves bundles[c] pointing to two dead-body wires. Compiling the following CX then calls scalar(c) on this wrong map, before Facts can skip Repeat(0,...).
sol.fix: Change reference-interpreter/src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile's qloop arm so a zero-trip body cannot mutate the successor bundle/lifetime/borrow/control environment. Either compile against an isolated environment and discard its dynamic effects, or omit its dynamic compilation after the existing static validation; retain function-entry qregion hoisting and all required static checks of dead bodies. §4.6 says 'body n times', so n=0 means zero body lifetime operations; §4.3 supplies 'n clean wires'; §5.3 explicitly requires adjoint 'versions renumbered'. Expected successor binding is the original one-wire c=0, not the two-wire dead definition. Add r8_zero_trip_lifetime_environment_does_not_escape in tests/r1_borrow.rs using the exact function and hashes above, plus tests/cli_xam.rs assertions for hash/check, forward and independently started adjoint at t=0/1 and the complex superposition, wires=1, no remaining workspace and reverse equals_entry=true. These parse/check success assertions fail now; after the fix every result must be the unchanged interface state and an externally entangled borrowed entry must also be preserved. Include nested zero loops and dead qcopy/qload/qborrow bindings followed by actual uses of the surviving binding. A dead body that redefines a still-live wire without releasing it must still fail static validation; changing this fixture's trip count to 1 while retaining scalar CX c must still reject the two-wire operand. No execution budget or certificate is involved.

sol.problem: Exact certificate composition silently treats a large unsigned multiplicity as negative. Decimal::mul_int(n:u128) constructs BigInt::from_i128(n as i128). For n=340282366920938463463374607431768211455 (u128::MAX), this is -1. Adapt tests/r1_linking.rs's existing client/callee fixture: give both forward:0 local error maps {"diamond":1}, callee inclusive {"diamond":1}, client inclusive {"diamond":"340282366920938463463374607431768211456"}, and client composition multiplicity "<INC_HASH>:forward:0":"340282366920938463463374607431768211455". Keep the existing signatures, pins, versions, matching target/dialect and bindings. Both independently constructed input certificates actually pass CLI check (client status unlinked, callee ok). By direct code trace, compose_certificates computes local(callee)*n + local(root) as 1*(-1)+1=0 and emits epsilon_total.diamond as JSON number 0; Object::link's subsequent parse accepts that nonnegative zero. The required sum is the exact decimal 340282366920938463463374607431768211456 (2^128). There is no CLI link command, so the composed result here is established by the explicit Rust code path, not claimed as a CLI execution. The same cast makes n=2^127 a negative multiplier. This is the already-implemented exact composition arithmetic, independent of the staged interval claim verifier.
sol.fix: Change reference-interpreter/src/exact.rs::Decimal::mul_int to construct a nonnegative BigInt from the complete u128 magnitude, without an intermediate signed cast; add an unsigned constructor if needed. Keep src/linking.rs::compose_certificates exact and do not cap multiplicities at i128::MAX. §9.3 says 'Linking = resolution, validation, certificate composition (§12.3), rebinding to closure hashes.' §12.3 specifies 'inclusive(R, key) = local(R, key) + Σ_callees n_c × inclusive(c, key_c)' and names method 'sum_over_multiplicities'; §9.1 permits large integers as decimal strings. Add an exact.rs unit test asserting Decimal::parse("1").unwrap().mul_int(u128::MAX).to_text() == "340282366920938463463374607431768211455"; it currently yields "-1". Cover 0, i128::MAX, 2^127 and u128::MAX and a fractional decimal as well. Add r8_unsigned_multiplicity_composition to tests/r1_linking.rs using its certify/region/client_text helpers: construct the two records and multiplicity in the problem, call Object::link(&[client,callee]).unwrap(), and assert composition.epsilon_total.diamond == Json::String("340282366920938463463374607431768211456".into()), followed by check_hashes(). The assertion currently sees Json::Number("0"); it must see the exact positive string after the fix. This test needs no execution budget, large allocation, schedule execution or interval verifier.
